proposal.description_medium: GAO estimated federal agencies incurred about $13.6 million for four Trump trips to Mar-a-Lago from February 3 through March 5, 2017. AP reported that about $60,000 of the total went directly to the resort. The estimate excluded certain classified information and employee salaries and benefits. proposal.description_long: The Government Accountability Office estimated that federal agencies incurred about $13.6 million in costs for four presidential trips to Mar-a-Lago from February 3 through March 5, 2017. The estimate included about $10.6 million in aircraft and boat operating costs and $3 million in temporary-duty expenses. The GAO highlights state that certain classified cost information and personnel salaries and benefits were excluded. The Associated Press’s contemporaneous report says about $60,000 of the total went directly to Mar-a-Lago. The GAO report also found that agencies did not consistently prepare required presidential-protection expenditure reports. These findings support a bounded account of four trips and certain federal costs. They do not establish total Trump Organization profit across every trip or property, nor do they substantiate the original description’s assertion of systematic profit on every official visit. The corrected title identifies the measured trips and the reported payment rather than presenting a limited estimate as a comprehensive profit calculation.

frozen_original.synopsis: Every time President Trump traveled to one of his private clubs or hotels, taxpayer money flowed into his personal businesses. Staff, security, and support personnel were billed for accommodations at Trump properties, creating a revenue stream that benefited the president directly. The Government Accountability Office found that the lack of cost controls and transparency made it impossible to fully audit how much public money went to Trump businesses. The pattern repeated at Mar-a-Lago, Bedminster, and Trump's Scottish golf courses. No prior president in modern history had so systematically profited from official travel.

staged_description.description_short: GAO estimated $13.6 million in federal costs for four 2017 Mar-a-Lago trips and identified about $60,000 in expenses paid to the resort.
staged_description.description_medium: A 2019 GAO report estimated agencies incurred about $13.6 million for Trump’s four Mar-a-Lago trips from February 3 through March 5, 2017. It identified about $60,000 in expenses paid to Mar-a-Lago, including Defense Department lodging and Secret Service operational space. This is not a measure of total Trump Organization profit across all travel or properties.
staged_description.description_long: The Government Accountability Office examined federal costs associated with four presidential trips to Mar-a-Lago between February 3 and March 5, 2017. GAO estimated that agencies incurred about $13.6 million for those trips, including approximately $10.6 million in government aircraft and boat operating costs and $3 million for temporary-duty expenses such as transportation, lodging, meals and incidentals. The estimate excluded certain classified information and salaries and benefits of personnel who would have been paid regardless of travel. GAO separately identified about $60,000 in expenses paid to Mar-a-Lago: roughly $24,000 for Defense Department lodging and $36,000 for Secret Service operational space. The report also found agencies had not consistently prepared required presidential-protection expenditure reports for Congress. These findings support a specific account of public travel costs and payments to the resort. They do not establish total profits received by the Trump Organization across every trip, every property or the full presidency. The title should describe the reported estimate and payment rather than generalize it as a comprehensive profit calculation.
